newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Technical glitch ends Shenzhen afternoon trade.
newsitem.headline: Technical glitch ends Shenzhen afternoon trade.

text.p: A technical malfunction halted trading on the Shenzhen A share market for the whole of the afternoon session on Thursday, exchange officials said.
Trading hours were not extended after the normal closing time because the malfunction of the telecommunications system had not been repaired at that time, they said.
At midday, the A share index rose 6.26 points or 2.04 percent to 312.33 on turnover of 3.27 billion yuan.
There was no trading on Wednesday and Thursday in the B market in line with the closure of the Hong Kong bourse because of the Christmas holiday. Trading will resume on Friday.
The officials said that they would publish on Friday morning official closing prices for A shares, funds and spot bonds and the A share index, after adjustments in the computer system.
The problem occurred in the telecommunications system of the Shenzhen Telecommunications office preventing communications between the exchange and its members in the city, they said.
Brokers said that the A share index rose in the morning because of speculative buying targeting cheap stocks that had posted heavy losses over the past few sessions.
Investors believe the A market had lost its downward momentum after sharp declines since Monday, they said.

Chemical fibre maker Shandong Weifang Hailong Co Ltd, which listed 15.60 million A shares in Shenzhen on Thursday, ended the morning session at 13.36 yuan per share, against an offer price of 1.80 yuan in 1988.

Television tube maker Shenzhen SEG Co Ltd floated 21.20 million A shares in Shenzhen today and closed the morning at 16.71 yuan compared with an offer price of 6.80 yuan per share earlier this month. The Shenzhen bourse has said the issue was 242 times over-subscribed.
Health Mineral Water surged 0.78 yuan at midday to its daily limit-up of 8.58 yuan on speculative demand by institutions.
